summary: CoAuthorMesh collects the institution's authors into an indexed TEMP table on an explicit *sql.Conn instead of matching them twice with `author_id IN (SELECT ...)`. COUNT(*) replaces COUNT(DISTINCT a1.work_id), which removes nothing because lancet_authorships has PRIMARY KEY (work_id, author_id). The table is dropped both on entry and on exit, so a cancelled run cannot break the next call on the same pooled connection.
reason: SQLite materialises the first reference to an IN-list but replays the second as a linear scan for every candidate row, making the cost (authorship rows) x (authors) rather than a lookup. On a 506k-authorship mirror an institution resolving to 3,649 authors and 12,020 rows meant roughly 44M list comparisons, and the command exceeded a 60s caller budget on every run. The TEMP table gives the second probe an index. It runs on an explicit connection because a TEMP table belongs to one SQLite connection and database/sql may hand the next statement a different one; one caller pins its pool to a single connection, but this function is handed a *sql.DB and cannot see that.
validated_outcome: Measured on a 506,201-authorship / 609,745-affiliation store, institution 'oxford': IN (SELECT ...) 29.9s, CTE narrowing the rows 28.4s, COUNT(*) without DISTINCT 28.7s, EXISTS against the affiliation index abandoned after 60s, indexed TEMP table 0.98s. Every completed variant returned 28,963 pairs, byte-identical under diff. go test ./internal/lancet/ adds five cases covering ranking, pair direction, the limit, three repeated calls on an unpinned pool, and a second institution after a first; six mutations fail them where the previous single-pair test passed all of them.
